messages:
mike: Heads up — seeing KMS decrypt errors in eu2 during GPU node onboarding, a bunch of nodes stuck in 'waiting-for-keys'. logs: `decrypt: access denied` :eyes:

irene: oh no. did the firewall policy change land recently?

mike: deploy-bot reported a policy roll that targeted ephemeral-egress ranges at 16:12 UTC. stack traces show connections to our keystore endpoints timing out, then KMS returning 403 for a subset of requests. snippet:

```
# kubelet logs
2026-02-15T16:14:02Z node-provisioner: attempting keystore decrypt
2026-02-15T16:14:02Z keystore-client: POST https://keystore-eu2.internal/Decrypt -> 403
2026-02-15T16:14:02Z node: fallback to onboard queue, retrying
```

sam: confirmed, I can repro from a test VM in eu2 with `curl -v` to keystore, hits a firewall reset. can someone @security?

irene: I'm on it. initial read — the egress ACL for the ephemeral subnet accidentally dropped a CIDR range used by our NATGW-to-keystore path. Looks like the policy intended to remove legacy ranges but the CIDR set in the commit missed the nat instance IP pool.

anna: What's the blast radius? Are only onboarding nodes affected or do running hosts also lose keystore access?

mike: Mostly onboarding/warmpool joins. Running nodes have cached KMS grants so they're OK for now. But onboarding failures mean autoscale can't replenish capacity and we start paying for fallback capacity in other regions. We're already seeing queue growth on the scheduler.

oncall-rota: Alerting: GPU pool eu2 capacity health degraded -> 42% available vs target 85%. This will impact latency SLAs for dedicated customers.

irene: Immediate mitigation plan: roll a temp allowlist for keystore/privatelink endpoints to the offending egress ACL (small PR + emergency change), and queue a rollback once we validate. Need approvals from infra and security.

sam: I can prepare the ACL patch: add exact /32s for the NAT instances and the privatelink IPs. Patch tested in staging. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4287 (wip).

irene: +1 from security if we scope to those IPs and add an expire tag. Also let's enable audit sampling reduction for the shipper so we don't overwhelm the siem while the allowlist is in place. That cuts egress to external SIEM by ~70%.

mike: Short-term approved. Sam/Tony do the change and ping me when live. For tracking: open an incident ticket and note cost exposure — cross-region cold starts are burning reserved standing by in us-west and ap-south.

sam: pushing the patch now, plan: apply at 16:40 UTC, monitor for 20m, rollback if any auth regressions.

deploy-bot: policy-rollout job started for PR#4287 at 16:41 UTC in eu2 (canary -> 3 subnets).

mike: After the allowlist, we should backfill nodes into the warmpool and pause cross-region failovers for 1 hour to avoid extra costs. Also open a follow-up: migrate keystore traffic to privatelink-only path + add NATGW healthcheck gating to the ACL rollout playbook.

irene: Agreed. I'll draft a remediation RFC: lock down ephemeral CIDR management, require 2nd approver for egress changes that affect keystore or kms scopes, and add an automated inventory check comparing commit CIDRs vs known NAT pools.

oncall-rota: Monitoring: keystore decrypt 403s dropping to near-zero after rollout. GPU pool queued joins decreasing. Keeping the incident open for 2h post-stable. :white_check_mark:
